messages:
maya: Hey team — first day. I'm running into an annoying issue: my app (running on host) can't connect to Postgres when Postgres is in docker-compose. I use Docker Desktop on macOS. When I run psql from host I can connect via unix socket /var/run/postgresql, but app says connection refused to 127.0.0.1:5432. From inside container, connecting to host with 127.0.0.1 doesn't work. Any recommended setup? I'm trying to follow the repo README but hitting network/host differences.

_tim: Congrats, welcome! Short answer: use host.docker.internal from inside containers to reach host services. If Postgres is inside a container, expose port and point host app at localhost:5432. If both are in containers, use the compose service name as the hostname (e.g., `db`)._

elaine: Add details: On macOS Docker Desktop there's no `--network=host` for Linux containers, so the common patterns are:
- host app, containerized Postgres => expose ports in the postgres service and connect to localhost on host.
- containerized app + containerized Postgres => use service name (e.g., `db`) on the default compose network.
- host app, containerized app, and Postgres on host => from inside containers use `host.docker.internal` to reach host.

Example docker-compose snippet (postgres + app in containers):
```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: passwd
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
  web:
    build: .
    depends_on:
      - db
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:passwd@db:5432/mydb
```

maya: Ah OK thanks — my mistake was running Postgres on the host and trying to connect from the container using 127.0.0.1. Switching to `host.docker.internal` from inside the container fixed it. For posterity here's the command that worked for me from inside the app container:
```
psql "postgresql://postgres:passwd@host.docker.internal:5432/mydb"
```

tim: Nice! Also, if you prefer to keep DB on host and dev without opening ports system-wide, you can use `socat` or an SSH tunnel, or set up a small forwarded port. But `host.docker.internal` is the simplest approach on Docker Desktop.

devops-bot: Docs: https://redwood.example.dev/internal/dev-environment#docker-networking :link

maya: Thanks all! :smile: Saved me a bunch of time. Will add a short note to the repo README.
